loras.name: Cinemagraph Motion
loras.description: Selective-motion cinemagraph look — the whole scene stays frozen except one detail, which loops its motion seamlessly.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: Turns a still image into a cinemagraph-style video: the camera is locked off and the entire scene stays completely frozen except for one selected detail, which loops its motion seamlessly (e.g. only a reflection, only drifting clouds, only falling tears).

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: A single reference image to animate — runs through the normal image-to-video flow, no special preprocessing.

instructions.title: Prompt
body: Trigger word CINEMAGRAPH_MOTION as the first token, then state the camera is locked-off/static, name everything that stays completely frozen, then name the one specific detail that moves and how, ending with 'seamless natural loop'.

Example: CINEMAGRAPH_MOTION, tripod locked-off static camera, zero camera movement, the parrot head remains completely frozen, beak locked in place, feathers locked in place, neck locked in place, body locked in place, sunglasses frame locked in place, palm trees, beach, ocean, sky, and background remain completely frozen, only the volcano eruption reflected inside the sunglasses lenses moves, in each lens the reflected volcano erupts dramatically — a powerful fountain of bright molten lava bursts and sprays high into the air from the crater, thick dark ash and billowing smoke plume upward and roll outward across the reflected sky, glowing rivers of orange lava stream and cascade down the volcano's slopes, showers of bright embers and sparks fly up and rain down, the eruption growing more intense and active, all animating continuously and vividly inside both lenses, the lens frames and parrot do not move at all, everything outside the moving reflection stays perfectly still, seamless natural loop.

instructions.title: Tips
body: Works best on short clips — 5–6 seconds.
LoRA strength ~1.0.

Out of scope: camera movement, character/body movement, complex dynamic scenes, or multiple moving subjects — it's trained on static, locked-off camera footage only. Describe everything except the one animated detail as frozen.
If using a negative prompt, exclude terms like camera movement, pan, tilt, zoom, parallax, whole image moving, background sliding, person moving.

enhancement_examples: CINEMAGRAPH_MOTION, tripod locked-off static camera, zero camera movement, the man, face, hair, clothing, beach, sky, and background remain completely frozen, only the beach reflection inside his sunglasses moves, reflected time-lapse of ocean waves roll and shimmer in the lenses, everything outside the glasses stays still, seamless natural loop.

CINEMAGRAPH_MOTION, tripod locked-off static camera, zero camera movement, the man and cow remain completely frozen, only the clouds in the sky move in fast time-lapse, clouds drift and roll across the sky, grass and foreground remain still, seamless natural loop.

CINEMAGRAPH_MOTION, tripod locked-off static camera, zero camera movement, the woman is frozen, her face, eyes, hair, clothing, seat, and airplane interior remain completely frozen, only the illustrated tear drops move downward along her cheeks like a cutout collage animation, seamless natural loop.

ic_loras.name: Clean Plate
ic_loras.description: Remove people and vehicles from a video and reconstruct the static background.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: Removes people, pedestrians and vehicles from a video, reconstructing the static background behind them for VFX/compositing clean plates. Best when subjects are partial or edge occluders with visible background — large first-person body parts filling the frame are out of scope.

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: A video with the subjects to remove. Trained at 1024×576/576×1024, 49 frames @ 25fps (min 8k+1 frames); validated up to 1920×1088.

instructions.title: Prompt
body: No trigger word — describe the desired empty scene, not a removal command. Name the specific people/objects to exclude.

Example: An empty clean plate of the exact same location: identical background, environment, structures and lighting as the source video, with no people, no humans, no figures, and no body parts such as heads, arms, hands or legs anywhere in the frame. No cast shadows or reflections of people. Static photorealistic footage, natural daylight, high detail.

instructions.title: Tips
instructions.body: LoRA strength 1.0. Name specific objects to remove in both positive and negative prompts for best results.

ic_loras.name: 3D Render to Photoreal
ic_loras.description: Turn a rough 3D viewport render (Blender blockout, game-engine viewport) into a photorealistic, cinematic video.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: Turns a rough grey 3D viewport render — Blender blockout, game-engine viewport or other CG/synthetic render — into a photorealistic, film-quality video, keeping the exact composition, camera move and layout of the input.

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: A 3D / CG render video (low-poly blockout, game viewport). An optional photoreal reference image can seed the first frame.

instructions.title: Prompt
body: Trigger word 3DREAL, then describe the photoreal result.
Example: 3DREAL a photorealistic cinematic harbor at dawn, fishing boats moored, soft volumetric light.

instructions.title: Tips
instructions.body: Composition and camera are locked to the input render; the prompt drives realism, materials and lighting. Download Strong (v2) or Light from the library card — Light is a subtler push.

ic_loras.name: Day to Night
ic_loras.description: Relight a daytime shot to look like it was filmed at night.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: Re-renders a daytime clip as the same shot at night. Composition, framing, camera move and subject motion are held frame-for-frame; your prompt only drives the new lighting, brightness and colour temperature.

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: A daytime video. Best near the training bucket: ~768×448 (or 448×768) at 97 frames (~4s), 24fps.

instructions.title: Prompt
body: No trigger word — describe the night scene and its light sources.
Example: A realistic nighttime scene. A cafe interior looking out at a dark city street, warm overhead lights casting amber reflections on the furniture.

instructions.title: Tips
body: LoRA strength 1.0.
Longer clips are possible but the relight can drift over the shot.
Indoor scenes or heavily artificial-light sources are outside the primary training distribution — outdoor daylight-to-night conversions are the strongest case.

ic_loras.name: Colorization
ic_loras.description: Add realistic color to a grayscale video.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: Restores natural colour to grayscale, monochrome or desaturated video, keeping the subject, framing and geometry identical.

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: A grayscale / B&W video. Training bucket is ~960×544 at 121 frames, 24fps.

instructions.title: Prompt
body: Trigger word COLORIZE, in a two-part shape — first describe the grayscale reference, then the colours you want: 'Reference shows {grayscale scene}. Edited shows the same scene with natural colors restored. COLORIZE {vivid colour description}.'

Example: Reference shows a wild rabbit on textured boulders in high-contrast monochrome. Edited shows the same scene with natural colors restored. COLORIZE a brown cottontail with warm tan and grey-brown fur on grey stone.

instructions.title: Tips
body: Keep the identity and framing wording identical between the two halves — change only the colour words.
LoRA strength ~1.0; don't render far above the training bucket or colour weakens.
Not a fix for blur, compression artifacts, noise or low resolution — pair with Deblur/Decompression/Upscale first if the source needs that too.

prompt_template.template: Reference shows {reference}. Edited shows the same scene with natural colors restored. COLORIZE {result}.

ic_loras.name: Decompression
ic_loras.description: Remove compression artifacts and restore a degraded video.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: Strips compression artifacts — macroblocking, chroma bleed, ringing, banding — from low-bitrate video. It is not a denoiser or upscaler.

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: A heavily compressed / low-bitrate video. Trained at 960×544 × 121 frames, 24fps.

instructions.title: Prompt
body: Trigger phrase ENHANCE QUALITY, in the two-part shape: 'Reference shows {scene}, heavily compressed with visible macroblocking, chroma bleed and ringing. Edited shows the same scene restored to high quality with sharp detail and clean edges. ENHANCE QUALITY {scene}.'

Example: Reference shows a rabbit between mossy boulders, heavily compressed with macroblocking and ringing. Edited shows the same scene restored, sharp and clean. ENHANCE QUALITY a reddish-brown rabbit between mossy grey boulders in soft daylight.

instructions.title: Tips
body: Use stage-1-only and render near the training resolution so the result stays aligned to the reference.
LoRA strength 1.0.
Not a general restoration model — it targets compression artifacts specifically, not defocus/motion blur, noise/grain, colorization or upscaling.

prompt_template.template: Reference shows {reference}, heavily compressed with visible macroblocking, chroma bleed and ringing. Edited shows the same scene restored to high quality with sharp detail and clean edges. ENHANCE QUALITY {result}.

ic_loras.name: Deblur
ic_loras.description: Sharpen and remove blur from a video.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: Regenerates out-of-focus footage in sharp focus, preserving subject, framing and geometry. Handles genuine defocus only — not motion blur, compression repair, denoise or upscale.

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: A defocused video, used directly as the reference. Trained at 960×544 × 121 frames, 24fps; renders well up to 1920×1088.

instructions.title: Prompt
body: Trigger word DEBLUR, in the two-part shape: 'Reference shows {scene}, heavily out of focus with soft defocused blur. Edited shows the same scene in sharp focus with crisp detail. DEBLUR {scene}.'
Example: Reference shows a butterfly on a pink flower, heavily out of focus. Edited shows the same scene in sharp focus. DEBLUR a vibrant butterfly resting on a bright pink flower.

instructions.title: Tips
body: LoRA strength 1.0; lower toward 0.8 if it over-sharpens.
Handles genuine defocus only — not motion blur, compression artifacts, denoising or super-resolution.
Extremely blurred content where detail is truly gone will be hallucinated rather than faithfully reconstructed — don't expect it to recover detail that isn't there.

prompt_template.template: Reference shows {reference}, heavily out of focus with soft defocused blur. Edited shows the same scene in sharp focus with crisp detail. DEBLUR {result}.

ic_loras.name: Cross-Eyed
ic_loras.description: Turn a close-up portrait's eyes permanently crossed (inward), keeping expression and framing.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: Turns a close-up portrait's straight eyes into permanent convergent strabismus (inward-turned / crossed eyes), while keeping facial expression, head movement, lighting and camera framing.

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: A close-up portrait video with straight eyes. Frame count must satisfy frames % 8 == 1 (e.g. 49); buckets 960×544×49 or 544×960×49.

instructions.title: Prompt
body: No trigger word — describe the crossed-eye result directly.

Example: A close-up portrait video of a man with permanent severe convergent strabismus. Both eyes are continuously turned inward toward the nose throughout the shot. The subject maintains natural facial expression, head movement, lighting, and camera framing.

ic_loras.name: Water Simulation
ic_loras.description: Add simulated water / fluid VFX to a scene.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: Adds water and fluid VFX — rivers, surf, rain, waterfalls, floods, splashes, spray, wet-surface speculars — onto a dry clip, keeping subject, clothing, pose, framing and background fixed.

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: A dry 'before' video at 24fps, 1920×1088 (or 1088×1920). Up to ~185 frames (~7.7s).

instructions.title: Prompt
body: Trigger phrase ADD WATER (required), in the two-part shape: 'Reference shows {dry scene}. Edited shows the same scene with water added. ADD WATER {water description}.'

Example: Reference shows a brown rabbit on mossy rocks. Edited shows the same scene with water added. ADD WATER a fast-flowing river with white foam rushing over and around the rocks behind the rabbit.

instructions.title: Tips
body: Be concrete about water type and motion.
LoRA strength ~1.2; use stage-1-only at native resolution to hold identity.

prompt_template.template: Reference shows {reference}. Edited shows the same scene with water added. ADD WATER {result}.

ic_loras.name: Ingredients
ic_loras.description: Keep a subject consistent across a video from a reference sheet.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: Drives a video from a reference sheet — a single composite image of characters, props and locations — so those elements stay visually consistent across the shot.

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: A reference sheet image laying out each element in its own panel. Training bucket 768×448, 121 frames, 24fps.

instructions.title: Prompt
body: Two labelled parts, no caps trigger — first describe each panel of the sheet, then describe the action: 'Reference sheet: {panels — characters, props, settings}. Generated video: {the action}.'
Example: Reference sheet: a 3D owl mascot shown from several angles; a bright grocery aisle. Generated video: a high-quality 3D animated commercial outside a modern 'FreshMart' store.

instructions.title: Tips
body: Give characters clean close-ups / turnarounds and larger panels — bigger, clearer panels carry over more faithfully and prevent identity drift.
LoRA strength ~1.4.
The generated video won't invent identities that aren't on the reference sheet — every character, prop or location it needs to render must have its own panel.
Suggested negative prompt: worst quality, inconsistent motion, blurry, jittery, distorted.

ic_loras.name: Instant Shave
ic_loras.description: Remove a beard / facial hair from a person in a video.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: Removes facial hair — beard, moustache, stubble — from a person in the video, while keeping identity, expression, motion, lighting and composition.

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: A reference video of the bearded subject. 960×544 (or 544×960) at 25fps, 33–121 frames; match the clip's fps to 25.

instructions.title: Prompt
body: Trigger word REMOVEBEARD, prepended, then describe the clean-shaven result.
Example: REMOVEBEARD completely smooth and clean-shaven, bare skin, no beard, no stubble, no facial hair.

instructions.title: Tips
body: LoRA strength 1.0; keep the training resolution to hold identity across the clip.
Identity can drift and residual stubble/shadow may persist on longer clips — shorter clips near the training length are more reliable.
Suggested negative prompt: beard, mustache, facial hair, stubble, worst quality, inconsistent motion, blurry, jittery, distorted.

ic_loras.name: Outpainting
ic_loras.description: Extend a video beyond its frame — widen it, change the aspect ratio, or fill new canvas around the shot.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: Extends a clip past its original frame. The source video sits on a larger canvas and the model paints the new surrounding region, matching the existing scene by default or following your prompt.

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: Any video. Drag the canvas edges to add space on any side (or drop in a corner to do two at once), and reposition the video within the canvas. Aspect-ratio presets (16:9 / 1:1 / 9:16 / 21:9) snap the canvas to that shape.

instructions.title: Prompt
body: No trigger word. Leave the prompt empty to just extend the scene, or write a plain description of what should appear in the new area.
Example: a sandy beach with crashing waves along the bottom of the frame.

instructions.title: Tips
instructions.body: Outpaint only (inpainting isn't supported here). LoRA strength 1.0. Keep additions modest — very large extensions are harder for the model to fill convincingly.

ic_loras.name: Greenscreen Avatar
ic_loras.description: Turn a vertical talking-head clip into the same person on a flat green chroma-key background, ready to composite.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: Transforms a vertical talking-head clip into the same person on a flat green chroma-key background — keyed and ready to composite onto any background. Sized for portrait/mobile formats (Reels, Shorts, TikTok).

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: A vertical (portrait) talking-head video — a person facing the camera.

instructions.title: Prompt
body: Describe the greenscreen talking head. Example: 'A person talking directly to the camera against a flat green chroma-key background. Natural lip sync, occasional blinks, subtle head movements. Soft natural lighting, photorealistic, sharp focus, stable framing.'

instructions.title: Tips
instructions.body: Vertical (portrait) clips. Stage-1-only at native resolution holds identity; raise the resolution factor if you have VRAM headroom.

ic_loras.name: Upscale (Refine)
ic_loras.description: Generative second-pass refinement — turn a soft / low-res clip into a cleaner, more detailed one.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: A generative refinement pass, not a plain upscaler — runs a soft or low-res clip back through LTX 2.3 to recover cleaner detail. Output can shift with settings, so it's meant as a second stage (e.g. after a stage-1-only run).

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: Bicubic-upscale your source to the target resolution first, then feed that as the reference video. Example: 640×360 → bicubic to 1280×720 → upscale pass.

instructions.title: Prompt
body: Trigger word: upscale (that's the whole prompt this LoRA expects).

instructions.title: Tips
instructions.body: Results depend on source quality, resolution, frame count and strength. Checkpoint is the 6250-step weights.

ic_loras.name: CrossView Prompt
ic_loras.description: Re-render a reference clip from a new camera angle — same scene and subject, different viewpoint. Uses a fixed camera-angle prompt vocabulary.

instructions.title: What it does
instructions.body: Acts as a virtual second camera: take a reference video and a short camera-angle prompt, and re-render the same scene from the requested viewpoint while keeping subject and content.

instructions.title: Input
instructions.body: A reference video of the scene you want to re-shoot from a new angle. No starting image needed.

instructions.title: Prompt
body: Every prompt must start with the trigger crossview. and follow this template (use the exact phrases):
crossview. new camera angle: {azimuth}, {elevation}, {distance}.
Azimuth: same angle · slightly to the left · slightly to the right · to the left · to the right · far to the left · far to the right
Elevation: lower · same height · higher
Distance: closer · same distance · further
Example: crossview. new camera angle: to the right, lower, closer.

instructions.title: Tips
instructions.body: Best on small, single-step angle changes. For a larger viewpoint shift, chain several small steps — feed the generated view back in as the new reference and apply another small angle. Views from behind are out of range (frontal sector only, about ±60°).
